direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale genuinely feels like it's from the Dhar Mann school of directing, as if Aaron Sorkin read a book on Directing 101 and just did whatever it told him to do, building the movie so formulaically, like something you would learn in film school, that it is the most basic, surface-level direction with no auteurism, style, or imagery that makes it feel like an Aaron Sorkin movie; the direction on a microscale is so surface level that it plays like a Dhar Mann sketch, forcing Aaron Sorkin's agenda without any research to back it up, and there is no chemistry in the cast whatsoever because everyone gives the most surface-level performances, minus Jeremy Strong, who is the only one who commits even though he is given such bad material to work with; the storytelling tells you what happened instead of showing you, spoon-feeding the audience like they're stupid and making them relive 2020 and 2021 when this movie would have been relevant in 2022 at the latest, since January 6th was almost six years ago now; the tension is actually negative because of how poorly it's directed, making moments that are supposed to be very serious kind of laughable since the tone feels like a feel-good '80s movie

performance.comments: Miscast in this role, as it doesn't play to her strengths and feels like she was cast for her looks; it should have been an ugly role, and she should have committed to that, but she tries so hard to be cute instead, and she has no chemistry with Jeremy Allen White whatsoever; her research is also incredibly surface level as it just feels like she read 'how to play a nerdy character' without looking more into the character

Basically shows up on set and plays himself, since I've seen him play this character so many times, and there's no transformation in this role whatsoever; it's fine because he's just using his natural self, but it's the most surface-level, generic character, like they didn't give him any direction and he just read the lines

The only one who actually commits to the role, but it feels like he just looked at videos of Mark Zuckerberg's mannerisms and voice to transform into the role and didn't do any further research; however, he's given such bad material that it negates the good work he does, since it's so surface level that you never get a sense of who Mark Zuckerberg is deep down, only the public persona everyone perceives him as
Literally just Bill Burr, as if they just told him to show up on set
One of the performances I did enjoy because she shows some range of emotion and is able to build chemistry with Strong
One of the performances I did enjoy as she has a sense of charisma in her performance

cast.comments: So surface level and forced, with a lot of forced chemistry that isn't good, making it feel like this movie is filled with non-actors, especially with these Aaron Sorkin-type characters directed by someone who went to the Dhar Mann school of directing

story.comments: The concept is genuinely stupid, trying so hard to attach itself to The Social Network without having any of the aspects to actually connect the two, telling the story from the perspective of journalists while barely being about Facebook or Mark Zuckerberg, and instead focusing on Frances Haugen and the Facebook whistleblower incident where a lot of negative information came out about Facebook and how it controls its audience, all handled so surface level that it feels like a movie they wanted to tell rather than one they needed to tell; the plot structure is somewhat linear but uses flashbacks and flash-forwards in such an amateur and stupid way, while breaking the movie up into poorly structured chapters makes it feel like it's being dumbed down for the audience, and the epilogue is so stupid that it feels like a fake movie; character writing is so bad, as Frances Haugen is supposed to be written as an ugly character, not physically, but as a socially anxious nerd who has trouble socializing, yet they oversexualize the role with dresses, dates, and romantic subplots while forcing the most stereotypical nerd tropes onto her, Jeremy Allen White's character is the most generic character ever, Mark Zuckerberg is written as his current public image instead of who he was at that time with no effort to show why he does what he does, and every other character, including Bill Burr's, is the most surface-level character ever; there are so many plot holes and cinema sins in the movie (like how she keeps saying she writes code as a data scientist and how they showed college basketball during Covid when it was cancelled)

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is genuinely bad, so unnatural and forced as it pushes Aaron Sorkin's agenda, and his signature shtick of inserting comedy or having people interject to make conversations feel natural only works when it attaches itself to well-written dialogue like The Social Network's, so it falls flat every time they do it here; the humor comes from that Aaron Sorkin shtick, which works somewhat, but the movie is honestly more laughable for how bad it is than for any of its actual jokes; the symbolism makes this the most forced agenda movie I've ever seen, as Aaron Sorkin clearly wanted to tell this story but didn't need to, forcing his message with no research to back it up through the most surface-level message delivery ever (the exact opposite of The Social Network), all while trying so hard to make January 6th the pinnacle of the movie when it happened almost six years ago and isn't relevant anymore; the foreshadowing makes the movie predictable as it leans way too far into tropes

score.comments: The exact opposite of The Social Network's score, as it is the most bland, feel-good piano Alexandre Desplat score ever; it is used very sparingly, and whenever it is used, it is always there to make the movie feel good, which is not what this movie is supposed to be since it's not an '80s feel-good movie

cinematography.comments: Feels very generic and amateurish, and genuinely feels like this movie is a generic student film

editing.comments: Terrible, as the flashback sequences use a bluish tint instead of actual black and white or gray, which is so stupid and amateur; many of the shots between sequences feel like they're from a student film, so many cuts aren't well stitched together, and the editing between timelines is so simple and formulaic

sound.comments: The ADR is atrocious because I genuinely can't understand what Mikey Madison is saying, 'jsafhdsfjfpodsfosdfi Facebook'

production_design.comments: Did a pretty good job painting the Facebook offices and how tech offices look, but it's so obvious they didn't shoot this movie in San Francisco

makeup.comments: They keep putting Mikey Madison in full-blown makeup when she's supposed to play this nerdy data scientist that doesn't understand people; it clearly shows they are trying to sexualize an ugly character, which is such a tonal mismatch

costumes.comments: They kept giving Mikey Madison's character these elegant, very sexualized date dresses when this is supposed to be a serious role, sexualizing the character to sell the movie when that's not what she is supposed to be, while also giving her stereotypical nerdy hand warmers

review.pacing: Just not good because of how bad the movie is and how it keeps jumping between timelines that don't connect well at all; they could have cut 10 minutes out of this movie, but honestly, forget cutting 10 minutes, they shouldn't have made the movie
review.climax: The most generic, forced, and unnatural climax ever, followed by an epilogue that genuinely feels like the end of a Dhar Mann video with the most forced '80s feel-good ending; they even put scenes after the 'what happened to them' cards you see at the end of biopics, when they should have just ended the movie once she was done with her testimony, shown what happened afterwards, and ended it there
review.tone: Feels like a phoned-in, surface-level, feel-good '80s movie when it is supposed to be serious, making it the antithesis of The Social Network; it tries to be a journalism movie about getting the facts and details and being very thorough, but does such a bad job of it because it's such a surface-level movie
review.final_notes: It's clear Sony gave up on this movie by changing it from a sequel to The Social Network to a companion piece, because even they knew it was going to suck, and thank God they did, since The Social Network's score would have gone down if this were a sequel, but as a companion piece, I'm keeping The Social Network's score the same; this movie basically feels like Spotlight at home
review.overall: Overall, 'The Social Reckoning' is so bad that it feels like Aaron Sorkin went to the Dhar Mann school of directing; if The Social Network is a movie about precision and everything clicking, this movie is an example of doing the bare minimum and nothing connecting, as Aaron Sorkin forces his agenda without any research to go deeper, presenting a shallow, surface-level movie that feels like the antithesis of The Social Network; it's very much a movie that was a want and not a need, and it should not have been made
